Severely limited experimental scope: only 4 small language models (≤227M parameters), no large-scale validation, narrow domain (language modeling only), different batch sizes complicate comparisons, no cross-domain evaluation

Practical improvements with real value: eliminates Adam dependency for stabilization, reduces memory overhead, uses efficient QR decomposition, and extends naturally to tensor-valued weights

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across four language models with proper statistical rigor (120 random search runs per method) demonstrating consistent improvements and validation of tensor extension
Well-written paper with clear motivation, logical structure, and good presentation including helpful visual comparisons (Figure 3)
weaknesses: Limited novelty of idealized KL-Shampoo scheme: Eq. (3) was previously proposed as theoretical example by Lin et al. (2019, 2024), and Vyas et al. (2025b) already considered similar expressions; main contribution is KL motivation rather than fundamentally new ideas
Labeled as 'preliminary results' in Figure captions, signaling incompleteness for a top-tier venue submission and raising concerns about readiness

Experimental scope limited to language modeling domain only; evaluation on vision, RL, or other domains would strengthen claims about broad applicability

Comprehensive empirical validation: extensive hyperparameter search (150 runs per method), consistent improvements across 4 LM architectures, thorough comparisons with F-Shampoo and VN-Shampoo variants demonstrating KL advantages

strengths: Well-motivated KL divergence perspective: Principled argument for why KL divergence is more appropriate than Frobenius norm for SPD matrix estimation, with clear connections to information geometry and quasi-Newton methods
Comprehensive theoretical framework: Five main claims with formal proofs establishing KL interpretation; elegant extension to tensor-valued settings and connections to matrix Gaussian whitening
Practical algorithm design: Clever use of EMA for eigenvalue estimation with outdated eigenbasis (Claim 4) enables QR decomposition, achieving SOAP-level per-iteration runtime
Rigorous experimental methodology: 150 random search runs per method, multiple architectures, state-of-the-art baselines, and extensive additional experiments comparing alternative divergences
Memory efficiency: Eliminates Adam overhead that both Shampoo and SOAP require; clear memory cost table provided
Clear presentation: Well-structured narrative with good motivation and logical flow of ideas
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: Two-sided Kronecker factorization (Eq. 4) previously explored by Lin et al. (2019, 2024) and Vyas et al. (2025b); main contribution is primarily a reframing under KL divergence rather than fundamentally new insights. KL perspective on quasi-Newton methods is also established in optimization literature

Modest empirical improvements: Gains over SOAP are marginal (e.g., ~3.31 vs ~3.32 test loss in Figure 1)—within plausible noise margins. No statistical significance testing despite 150 runs; no confidence intervals or p-values provided

Lack of convergence analysis: No convergence guarantees or rates for practical algorithms. Gap between idealized KL-Shampoo (coupled equations in Claim 2) and practical implementation (Eq. 5 with EMA and outdated eigenbasis) not rigorously bridged. No error bounds for outdated eigenbasis approximation

Limited experimental scope: Only language model training evaluated; no vision, RL, or other domains. Models are small-scale (123M-227M); scalability to modern LLMs (7B+) unclear. Different batch sizes and datasets across models complicate comparison

Implementation and reproducibility issues: Numerical precision concerns (float32 to bfloat16 casting in footnote 1 not discussed); hyperparameter sensitivity unexplored; no ablation studies; no released code; difficult to reproduce with 150-run random search

Weak analysis of core limitation: Figure 5 shows one-sided vs two-sided empirically, but mathematical reason for one-sided failure not deeply explained. Why does Kronecker structure 'not adequately solve' the KL problem? Limited theoretical insight beyond empirical observation

No convergence or regret analysis: Equations (5) and practical algorithm lack formal guarantees. How well do single-sample gradient approximations satisfy the KL optimality conditions (Eq. 4)? No analysis of accumulated errors from approximations
Missing recent baselines: Muon mentioned in references but not experimentally compared. No evaluation against other recent Kronecker-factored methods or natural gradient variants
Unexplained phenomenon: Authors state KL-Shampoo outperforms KL-SOAP as 'surprising' without explanation, suggesting incomplete understanding of their own results
Statistical rigor: Claims of 'consistent outperformance' with marginal improvements; differences often within 1% of test loss; no significance testing despite statistical power from 150 runs

strengths: Novel and well-motivated KL divergence perspective on second-moment estimation that respects SPD constraint, with clear theoretical justification
Rigorous theoretical contributions with five formal claims and complete proofs characterizing optimal solutions for covariance estimation
Comprehensive empirical evaluation with 150 random search runs per method across multiple architectures (GPT, RWKV, Llama, MoE), reducing variance and enabling robust comparisons
Practical algorithmic innovations including EMA scheme for eigenvalue estimation with outdated eigenbasis and QR integration, achieving SOAP-level runtime
Memory efficiency gains by eliminating Adam overhead and competitive performance without step-size grafting
Clean distinction between idealized theoretical schemes and practical implementations with systematic ablations (e.g., Fig. 4 on EMA vs. instantaneous eigenvalues)
Natural extension to tensor-valued weights demonstrated empirically, showing framework generality
weaknesses: Empirical scope limited to language model pretraining on relatively small models (123M-227M); no evaluation on vision, other NLP tasks, or different domains
Modest practical improvements over SOAP (1-3% on test loss); unclear if benefits persist at 10B+ scale or different optimization regimes
Theoretical gaps: no convergence analysis for practical EMA scheme; gap between idealized Eq. (4) and practical Eq. (5) not formally analyzed; no convergence rates
Confounded comparisons especially in Fig. 5: all methods benefit from QR+EMA engineering improvements, making it difficult to isolate pure effect of KL divergence choice
Surprising result that KL-Shampoo outperforms KL-SOAP lacks explanation—intuition for why removing Adam in eigenbasis improves optimization is missing
Baseline implementation inconsistencies: SOAP uses official implementation while KL-methods use authors' implementation; unclear if this affects results
Missing ablations on damping parameter κ, QR update frequency sensitivity, and β₂ parameter effects; limited analysis of which design choices drive performance
Reproducibility concerns: code not provided, some implementation details underspecified (e.g., precision handling), hyperparameter search distributions not fully specified
No end-to-end wall-clock training time comparisons; experiments limited to ~150-300 minutes, unclear if improvements hold over full training
Limited novelty of practical techniques: QR decomposition from SOAP (Vyas et al. 2025a); EMA scheme is standard technique applied in new context
